results.answer: Skipping this month means the next instalment will not be taken, and the SIP will continue as normal from the following month. Your already purchased units stay invested and keep moving with the market.
Cancelling stops future instalments but the money already invested stays invested and continues to grow with the fund.
If an auto-debit fails, the fund house does not charge a penalty, but your bank may levy a fee for the failed debit. The exact fee depends on your bank.
In this demo you can pause a SIP for 1 to 3 months. After the pause period the SIP automatically restarts at the same amount.

Yes, after you pause a SIP it will automatically restart after the pause period ends. In this demo you can pause for 1 to 3 months, and the SIP resumes at the same amount. The restart happens without any extra action from you.
You can lower the SIP amount down to the fund's minimum, which is ₹100 in this demo.
Yes, after cancelling a SIP you can start a new one later, which may require a new mandate. Your previously invested units remain in the fund.
Stopping or pausing a SIP does not trigger any tax; tax applies only when you redeem units.
Pausing a SIP does not attract any exit load; exit load applies only when you redeem units.

Cancelling the mandate at your bank stops the auto‑debit, so the next SIP instalment will fail (see R8). The failed payment may just result in a bank fee and could eventually lead to the fund house cancelling the SIP if it happens repeatedly (see R6).
If you pause today, the request may take a few working days, so the instalment scheduled for tomorrow could still be processed.
Yes, lowering the amount keeps the SIP active as long as the new amount is above the minimum (₹100 in this demo). The SIP continues with the reduced instalment amount.
